A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WorldWander and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original EgoExo-8K evaluations, component ablations, qualitative results, and a user study with 630 valid responses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds an untuned ReCamMaster comparison, timestep and LoRA-rank ablations, and interaction examples.

M1.justification: The Wan2.2-5B backbone, LoRA adaptation, clean conditional latents, collaborative attention, shared temporal position encoding, and flow-matching objective remain unchanged. Reference-conditioned ego-to-exo generation is already present in v1; expanded explanations and corrected task-variable labels do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the synthetic GTA-5 and real-world EgoExo-8K subsets for bidirectional perspective translation. Dynamic navigation and human-object interaction already appear in v1's dataset coverage; v2's cooking and manipulation examples in Figure 8 provide additional cases within that scope.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds an untuned ReCamMaster comparator for synthetic scenarios alongside the retained fine-tuned version. AnyV2V, I2VEdit, TrajectoryCrafter, and the existing fine-tuned ReCamMaster comparisons remain; newly discussed ego/exo methods are not actually evaluated.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce a uniform-timestep variant, LoRA ranks 64 and 128 alongside the retained rank 80, and a ReCamMaster comparison without fine-tuning. Existing metrics, clip settings, held-out triplet counts, and user-study sample size remain unchanged. Removing the stated 6,000-step budget does not establish that training changed.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing analyses with timestep and LoRA-rank tests in Table 2, a fine-tuning control in Table 1, and human-object interaction cases in Figure 8. These are focused additions; the earlier component ablations, convergence comparison, failure cases, and out-of-domain gallery are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added result rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Previously reported scores in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged. Added results include untuned ReCamMaster synthetic FVD values of 738.7 for exo-to-ego and 915.7 for ego-to-exo, uniform-timestep and rank-64/128 results, and Figure 8 interaction examples. These are additional results under additional conditions, not improved same-setting WorldWander scores.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematical formulation remains unchanged, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation. v2 adds the standard inference ODE in Section 3 to explain the existing flow model; the remaining equations correspond to v1 after renumbering.

C1.justification: v2 substantially revises the novelty claims: v1 broadly introduces ego/exo translation and claims no existing paired dataset, whereas v2 acknowledges prior datasets and emphasizes bidirectional dynamic navigation, reference-guided synthesis, and the first dynamic open-world wandering benchmark. The core framework and performance claims remain, although several novelty passages incorrectly reverse ego/exo direction labels.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the rationale that typically fixed perspectives make camera parameters less important with an argument about geometry-free generalization across moving cameras. v2 also interprets the new fine-tuning control as evidence of dataset usefulness and the rank sweep as supporting rank 80. The appendix limitations concerning physical consistency and limited human diversity are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents the GTA-5 two-player/spectator collection protocol, names the real-world cameras, and reconciles the camera-mounting description with the earlier appendix. It adds approximately two-day training and three-minute inference times but removes the exact 6,000-step training budget. The code-access link and most implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The general video-diffusion survey is replaced by a dedicated exo-to-ego related-work section, with added discussion and citations concerning 4Diff, EgoWorld, EgoExo4D, H2O, and TACO. v2 positions the contribution against prior static, unidirectional, or auxiliary-input settings and explains exclusions from direct comparison, substantially revising the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, task formulation, and dataset narrative are extensively rewritten. Supplementary Sections 7–11 become Appendices A–E before the bibliography, and acknowledgements are added. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, redistributing and resizing figures and tables throughout. v2 adds the positional-encoding illustration and interaction examples, reorganizes the dataset mosaics, and expands both results tables with rows and fine-tuning markers. Most existing comparison and appendix images are retained.

improvement.justification: The added timestep/rank ablations and ReCamMaster fine-tuning control provide useful support for existing design choices, while the focused related work and collection details make the contribution easier to assess. The net gain is limited: headline results remain unchanged, inconsistent direction labels weaken the novelty discussion, and omission of the exact training-step budget reduces reproducibility.
